rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration to establish whether combining RNA and image data improves performance. This configuration uses pca_n2000 for RNA, resnet50 for images, and simple concatenation fusion, which clarifies the impact of multimodal integration. It is the best use of the first experiment to explore the core hypothesis of multimodal benefits without overcomplicating the setup.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal configurations with concat fusion and no aggregation achieve 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (a key design choice in multimodal models) improves performance, clarifying if fusion method is critical. It directly builds on the previous configuration while exploring a high-impact variation, balancing exploitation of the multimodal direction with exploration of fusion strategies.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile with pca_n2000 and resnet50 has validation accuracy ~0.526. This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with a more advanced image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) in the same setup, clarifying whether image encoder choice is critical. It addresses a key design decision (encoder architecture) that could significantly impact performance, while maintaining consistency with prior multimodal singleprofile experiments.

The existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder (config_022) outperforms resnet50. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted (while keeping the high-performing image encoder and RNA encoder) improves validation accuracy. It clarifies the importance of fusion strategy with the current best image encoder, balancing exploitation of the strong image encoder and exploration of fusion methods.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l as image encoder (config_022) outperforms resnet50, and concat fusion (config_022) is better than weighted. This experiment tests multiprofile (untested in top-performing configurations) with the same image encoder and aggregation method, clarifying if multiprofile improves performance while maintaining the effective components from config_022. It balances exploration of profile settings with exploitation of proven components.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile setups with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion (config_024) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.6287). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 in the same multiprofile setup (with resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and concat fusion) improves performance. This clarifies the impact of RNA encoder choice on multiprofile performance, an important design decision with sparse prior evidence.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings and scvi_n200 RNA encoder (config_030) achieve high accuracy (0.6315). This experiment tests whether using the more powerful imagenet_vit_l image encoder with weighted fusion (instead of concat) improves performance, clarifying the impact of image encoder choice and fusion method. It balances exploitation of the scvi_n200 RNA encoder (a strong performer) with exploration of image encoder and fusion variations, which are critical design choices with uncertain optimal configurations.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (0.706). This experiment tests transformer aggregation (a more complex method) with the same RNA and image encoders and weighted fusion, clarifying whether transformer aggregation further improves performance. It balances exploitation of proven components (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, weighted fusion) with exploration of aggregation methods, which are critical design choices with uncertain optimal settings.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile setups with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039) achieve high validation accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether using the scgpt RNA encoder (instead of scvi_n200) with the same effective components (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) can further improve performance, clarifying the importance of RNA encoder choice. It directly builds on the strongest prior direction while exploring a key design decision.

Existing evidence shows that using transformer aggregation with weighted fusion (config_039) achieves high validation accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether using concat fusion instead of weighted fusion with the same transformer aggregation and scvi_n200/imagenet_vit_l setup clarifies the importance of fusion method. It directly addresses a key design choice with strong prior evidence, balancing exploration of critical parameters while building on the promising direction of transformer aggregation.
